text:
alice (support): heads-up: multiple customers reporting spikes of 5xx from the hosted API in us-west1 since ~2025-03-14T22:00Z. errors look like control-plane -> auth/session timeouts and routing failures. request-id examples: rq_9f3a2, rq_9f3a9. one customer pasted this response body:

{
  "error": "control_plane_error",
  "detail": "auth session validation timeout"
}

alice (support): impact: create-session and generate endpoints returning 502/503. some customers hitting rate limits and also billing alerts, raising escalations.

ben (oncall): :rotating_light: thanks — are these correlated with any deploys or infra jobs? can you paste a repro curl and one request-id from logs? I’ll start by checking control-plane pod errors and DB metrics.

alice (support): repro (customer provided):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-xxx" \  -d '{"model":"rw-large","prompt":"hello"}'
```
response: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"control_plane_5xx","msg":"auth/session service timed out validating token"}

carla (infra): looking at infra metrics now. there was a scheduled full backup on config-db primary at 2025-03-14T21:58Z that overlapped with a config publish spike. config-db CPU and I/O spiked to 95% for ~7m. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/g/config-db?from=2025-03-14T21:50Z&to=2025-03-14T22:10Z

carla (infra): routing-policy service depends on config-db for policy resolution. when config-db p99 reads hit 450ms we started seeing routing-policy timeouts which propagate as 5xx to control-plane API. also noticed session-token-cache TTL was recently rotated to 30s in last week's change — increased cache churn.

dave (eng-runtime): that cache TTL change could cause thundering herd on session validation. routing-policy fallback currently throws 500 if store read fails. two quick mitigations: 1) make routing-policy fall back to last-known-good cached policy (best-effort) 2) temporarily increase session-token-cache TTL to 300s.

ben (oncall): can you share the commands to check pods / tail logs? I’ll pull live traces and correlate request ids.

carla (infra):
```
kubectl -n control-plane get pods -l app=routing-policy
kubectl -n control-plane logs deploy/routing-policy --since=10m | grep "ERROR" -A3
# check db slow queries
psql -h config-db-primary -U redwood -c "select pid, query, now()-query_start as duration from pg_stat_activity where state!='idle' order by duration desc limit 10;"
```

ben (oncall): found multiple routing-policy exceptions with trace ids span-0a3b.. span shows configdb read timeout after 500ms socket deadline. also many auth/session service calls showing upstream timeout: context deadline exceeded. attaching sample log: 
```
[2025-03-14T22:02:12Z] routing-policy ERROR request_id=rq_9f3a2 configdb read timeout after 500ms
[2025-03-14T22:02:12Z] auth-service WARN request_id=rq_9f3a2 session validation timed out (cache-miss)
```

support-bot: alert: 17 incidents aggregated in last 10m for control-plane 5xx in us-west1. page: #oncall:ben.

dave (eng-runtime): pre-approved quick fix: patch routing-policy to use cached fallback and return 200 with degraded routing instead of 500. I'll push a hotfix canary to 2 pods now. also adding backoff + retry in auth validation (2 retries, short sleep).

deploy-bot: Deployed routing-policy hotfix to control-plane/us-west1 canary (replicas: 2 -> 4) at 2025-03-14T22:12:03Z.

carla (infra): rolling back non-critical config publish that spiked writes to config-db (config service release id c-pub-2025-03-14-07) and scaling config-db read replicas + raising connection pool from 50 -> 150. doing that now.

carla (infra): also running a cache warm-up script to prime routing-policy caches against last-known policies to reduce cold reads:
```
# warm up routing policy cache
python scripts/warm_policy_cache.py --env prod --region us-west1 --concurrency 10
```

alice (support): added customer repro steps and request-ids to the escalation ticket, pinging impacted customers with ETA ~30m.

ben (oncall): noticed error rate drop after deploy and DB scaling. p50 latency down, 5xx rate from 6.8% -> 0.9% in 12m. still watching.

carla (infra): config-db metrics look stable now. I/O settles, slow query count down. connection pools warmed.

dave (eng-runtime): hotfix applied cluster-wide. changed routing-policy behavior: on config-store timeout return last-known policy and add header X-Routing-Degraded: true. also increased session-token-cache TTL to 300s and added retries for token validation. pushing PR for proper rollout: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-policy/pull/789

alice (support): customers updated — one customer confirmed recovered for their flows. they got transient duplicate logs but no billing overages.

ben (oncall): open action items:
- carla: postmortem on config-db backup schedule + autoscaling gap
- dave: code change to avoid fail-open/closed ambiguity and add circuit breaker for config-store reads
- infra+eng: consider sticky token cache per region to avoid global thundering
- support: follow up with customers impacted and escalate to CS manager if needed

alice (support): thanks everyone. closing this thread once postmortem posted. :thumbsup:

support-bot: incident resolved: control-plane 5xx spike (auth/session + routing policy) — duration ~22m. follow-up: postmortem required.
